gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Sharp, wiry and a bit sci-fi, Megrim draws every stroke at a single measured weight. And Noto Sans Tai Viet follows with short ascenders and a lofty lowercase, so a long page would read like easy, friendly plain sans.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-takri: Megrim draws every stroke at the same thin, measured width, angular and futuristic. Noto Sans Takri settles underneath with a high-waisted lowercase and generously unclosed curves, so a longer passage would flow in a smooth, contemporary rhythm without tiring the eye.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supplement: Megrim looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to one line width, angular and futuristic from the first letter. And Noto Sans Tamil Supplement, with round forms like open parentheses and a stocky middle band, can go a touch larger than you might expect.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Megrim has no thick-thin swell at all, just angular lines that look nothing like pointed-brush strokes. Noto Sans Tangsa handles the everyday work, offering wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems, while Megrim saves its energy for the display moments.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-telugu: Noto Sans Telugu reads with a high-set midline and open counters.  Next to Megrim's thick-only outlines, a longer passage would feel connected to the surrounding space and steady, never cramped or fussy.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Megrim is angular and futuristic, cut like strips of equal width. Noto Sans Thai Looped has bold-looking lowercase with spacious gaps at the curve ends, so extended reading would feel clean, sturdy and surprisingly relaxed.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Noto Sans Tirhuta reads big and open, its terminals cut back to leave a wide gap. Beside Megrim's quiet, level beat with no accents of weight, a longer passage would move along smoothly and cleanly, like plain sans should.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-vai: Megrim has tubular, wire-like letterforms, angular and futuristic in a way that looks bent from metal. Noto Sans Vai gives words the feel of solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space between curve ends and stems, so extended reading stays approachable.
gen-megrim-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-square: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square reads crisp and approachable, with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes sharp and a soaring x-height. Megrim, with horizontals as thick as its verticals, sets the angular tone above.
gen-megrim-gf-numans: Megrim traces angular, futuristic letters as thick-only outlines, a display face that looks drawn with a single wire. Its edge against Numans is the strongest quality here: sans with widely spaced, coiled lowercase.
